paper.citation: Stefan Wager and Susan Athey (2018). Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 113(523):1228–1242. DOI 10.1080/01621459.2017.1319839
paper.title: Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_version: arXiv:1510.04342v4, submitted revision 2017-07-10; PDF title date July 11, 2017; 48-page prepublication version of the JASA article
paper.source_locator: arXiv:1510.04342v4 Appendix B, PDF p.31, unnumbered paragraph beginning “We are in a randomized controlled trial”, equation Yi=2WiAi+epsilon_i and noise/Bernoulli definitions

mechanism.name: 随机处理与稀有个体响应
generation_equations: B~Bernoulli(0.05), epsilon~N(0,0.1**2), independent of X,A and each other.
Y=2*A*B+epsilon. Source W is treatment A here; source A_i is the latent response indicator B, not a baseline covariate.

latent_variables.name: B
latent_variables.distribution: Bernoulli(0.05), independent of X, A and Gaussian noise

sampling.dependence: All ten observed covariates are irrelevant; effective_dimension=0 and high_dimensional=false. Latent B is never returned. No observed covariate interaction/nonlinear mean is claimed; mixture non-Gaussianity is described separately. Independent treatment/noise random draws conditional on covariates; no clusters or panel structure.

assumptions: Consistency and no interference across independent individuals.
Conditional exchangeability given observed baseline X under the declared synthetic assignment.
Pointwise positivity; no uniform overlap bound claimed for unbounded Gaussian logistic settings.

properties.notes: All ten observed covariates are irrelevant; effective_dimension=0 and high_dimensional=false. Latent B is never returned. No observed covariate interaction/nonlinear mean is claimed; mixture non-Gaussianity is described separately.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full declared covariate population; treatment 1 versus 0; population, not sample-conditional, target.

truth.expression: E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full declared covariate population; treatment 1 versus 0; population, not sample-conditional, target.
truth.derivation: E[Y(1)-Y(0)]=2*E[B]=2*0.05=0.1. Individual responses are 0 or 2; the conditional mean effect is constant 0.1. The treated outcome is a normal mixture, not N(0.1,0.01).

adaptations: Population ATE uses the constant source conditional mean effect 0.1; source pointwise forest-inference experiment is not reproduced.
Source treatment indicator is named A in the observed output; no scientific change.
Independently implemented Python/NumPy sampler; source estimator fitting and large simulation replications are outside this collection task.
Rename source rare-response A_i to latent B to avoid confusion with treatment; B is not exported.
